PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

Verb aspect shows whether an action is in progress. In this sub-strand you will identify and use the present progressive, made with am, is or are plus a verb ending in -ing, and the past progressive, made with was or were plus a verb ending in -ing. You will listen for these forms, build sentences about technology and cyber safety, and use them when you speak and write.

## Strand 7.0: Technology - Cyber Safety
Sub-strand 7.3.1: Grammar in Use: Word Classes (Verb Aspect)
Suggested lessons: 3

## What this sub-strand covers
• Present Progressive Aspect
• Past Progressive Aspect

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 English Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Theme 7.0 Technology - Cyber Safety, Sub-strand 7.3.1 Word Classes: Verb Aspect

PAGE 2: Learning outcomes

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) identify the present and past progressive forms of the verb in oral and written texts for communication
b) use the present and past progressive aspect correctly in oral and written contexts for self- expression
c) adopt the use of the present and past progressive aspect in communication

## Key inquiry questions
1. Why is it important to show when something happened?
2. How do we tell an action is or was happening?

PAGE 3: How we will learn

## Learning experiences
• listen to a radio or TV programme and identify the present and past progressive forms
• give examples of actions in the present and past progressive aspect
• use a given list of verbs to form sentences in the present and past progressive aspect collaboratively
• watch a video and write examples of the present and past progressive aspect in a notebook
• role-play or simulate an event in which they use the present and past progressive forms forms
• complete a sentences using words in their present and past progressive aspect correctly

## Core competencies
• Self-efficacy: This is promoted as the learner confidently uses present and past continuous forms in sentences correctly.
• Learning to Learn: It is developed as the learner identifies present and past continuous forms from newspaper and magazine articles.

## Values
• Responsibility is cultivated as the learner takes up roles during role play and simulation activities with peers.
• Integrity: It is enhanced as the learner observes honesty when searching for information in newspaper or magazines articles.

## Pertinent and contemporary issues
• Digital Literacy: It is enhanced as the learner uses and manipulates digital devices to watch a video or listen to programmes featuring aspect.

## Links to other learning areas
• The learner can connect the concept of past and present progressive aspect to their learning in Kiswahili.

PAGE 4: Lesson 1: The present progressive aspect

LESSON 1: THE PRESENT PROGRESSIVE ASPECT
========================================

## What you will learn
• Form the present progressive with am, is or are and a verb ending in -ing.
• Spell -ing forms correctly.
• Use the present progressive for an action happening now.

Curriculum outcomes: a) identify the present and past progressive forms of the verb in oral and written texts for communication; b) use the present and past progressive aspect correctly in oral and written contexts for self- expression

## Introduction
Look around the classroom. One learner is writing, another is listening, and perhaps the teacher is charging a tablet. Those actions are happening now. English has a verb form for that moment.

## Notes

### What the present progressive tells us
The present progressive aspect, also called the present continuous, shows that an action is in progress. It has two parts: a present form of be, and the main verb with -ing.

- I **am** typing.
- Hassan **is** charging the tablet.
- The pupils **are** watching a lesson.

Use **am** with I. Use **is** with he, she, it or one person's name. Use **are** with you, we, they and plural names.

PAGE 5: Lesson 1: The present progressive aspect — How to spell the -ing form

### How to spell the -ing form
- Most verbs add -ing: watch → watching, download → downloading, play → playing.
- If the verb ends in a silent e, drop the e: share → sharing, use → using, care → caring, take → taking.
- If a short verb ends with one vowel and one consonant, double the consonant: chat → chatting, sit → sitting, stop → stopping. Do not double the consonant in help → helping or talk → talking.

### When to use it
Use this aspect for an action happening at the moment of speaking. Words such as now, at the moment, look and listen often sit beside it. Look, Zawadi is closing the laptop.

A habit uses the simple present, not the progressive. Zawadi closes the laptop every evening. That sentence is about a regular action, not about this moment.

PAGE 6: Lesson 1: The present progressive aspect — Negatives and questions

### Negatives and questions
Put not after am, is or are. She is not sharing her password. In a question, move am, is or are in front of the subject. Are they downloading a game? Is he chatting with a stranger?

When you listen to a radio or television programme, listen for is or are followed by a word ending in -ing. That pattern is the present progressive.

PAGE 7: Lesson 1: The present progressive aspect — Example 2

## Key words
• progressive aspect — the verb form that shows an action in progress, also called the continuous
• present progressive — am, is or are plus a verb ending in -ing, for an action happening now
• helper verb — a verb such as am, is or are that helps the main verb

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Change to the present progressive: The children watch a cyber-safety video.

Working:
1. The subject The children takes are.
2. watch adds -ing.
3. Join the two parts.

Answer: The children are watching a cyber-safety video.

## Worked examples

### Example 2
Spell the -ing form of share, chat and download.

Working:
1. share ends in silent e, so drop e.
2. chat is a short verb ending in one vowel and one consonant, so double t.
3. download just adds -ing.

Answer: sharing, chatting, downloading

PAGE 8: Lesson 1: The present progressive aspect — Actions happening now

## Activity: Actions happening now
You will need: Verb cards: type, share, use, sit, take, chat, download, help, Notebook

1. In groups, pick four verb cards and write a present progressive sentence for each one about using a phone or computer safely.

2. One learner acts an action, such as typing or closing a laptop, while the group says the sentence: She is typing.

3. Read the sentences aloud and underline am, is or are and the -ing word.

4. Correct any spelling of the -ing form together.

PAGE 9: Lesson 1: The present progressive aspect — Summary

## Practice

1. Complete: Look! Father ________ (charge) the phone.

2. Write the -ing form of use, stop and play.

3. Which sentence shows an action happening now: I download songs every Friday, or I am downloading a song now?

4. Make the sentence negative: They are sharing the password.

## Answers to practice

1. is charging

2. using, stopping, playing

3. I am downloading a song now.

4. They are not sharing the password.

## Summary
• The present progressive is am, is or are plus a verb ending in -ing.
• Drop a silent e, and double a final consonant in short verbs such as chat.
• Use it for actions in progress now, not for regular habits.

PAGE 10: Lesson 2: The past progressive aspect

LESSON 2: THE PAST PROGRESSIVE ASPECT
=====================================

## What you will learn
• Form the past progressive with was or were and a verb ending in -ing.
• Use it for an action that was in progress at a time in the past.
• Join a past progressive action to a shorter past action with when or while.

Curriculum outcomes: a) identify the present and past progressive forms of the verb in oral and written texts for communication; b) use the present and past progressive aspect correctly in oral and written contexts for self- expression

## Introduction
Yesterday at six o'clock you were not frozen in one finished act. You were eating, walking or reading. The past progressive lets you talk about that unfinished moment in the past.

PAGE 11: Lesson 2: The past progressive aspect — Building the past progressive

## Notes

### Building the past progressive
The past progressive uses **was** or **were** plus the -ing form of the main verb. The spelling of the -ing form follows the same rules as in the present progressive.

- I **was** reading a message.
- He **was** uploading a picture.
- You **were** waiting for the page to open.
- The children **were** using the laptop together.

Use **was** with I, he, she, it and one name. Use **were** with you, we, they and plural names.

### What it means
This aspect shows an action that was already happening at a certain time in the past. At 7 o'clock I was watching a learning video. The video was in progress at that time. It does not tell us the moment the video finished.

PAGE 12: Lesson 2: The past progressive aspect — Key words

### A long action and a short action
A shorter finished action often interrupts the longer one. Use the past progressive for the longer action and the simple past for the short one.

- I **was downloading** a file when the lights **went** off.
- While Mother **was cooking**, my brother **sent** a message to a stranger.

**While** often introduces the longer action. **When** often introduces the shorter one. Both actions can be progressive if they happened side by side: While I was typing, my sister was drawing.

### Negatives and questions
I was not chatting online. Were you using earphones? After a question, answer with the same helper: Yes, I was. No, they were not.

Do not mix the helpers. She were typing and They was typing are not correct. Match was and were to the subject.

## Key words
• past progressive — was or were plus a verb ending in -ing, for an action in progress in the past
• interrupt — to break into a longer action with a shorter one
• while — a linking word often used for two actions happening at the same time

PAGE 13: Lesson 2: The past progressive aspect — What was happening?

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Join the ideas: Neema was closing the laptop. A message appeared.

Working:
1. The closing was already in progress, so keep the past progressive.
2. The message was a short finished event, so use the simple past appeared.
3. Link them with when.

Answer: Neema was closing the laptop when a message appeared.

## Worked examples

### Example 2
Choose was or were: The two boys ________ searching for a safe website.

Working:
1. The subject is plural: two boys.
2. Plural subjects take were.

Answer: were

## Activity: What was happening?
You will need: A short radio or video clip chosen by the teacher, or the class script below, Notebook

1. Listen to a short programme, or listen as two learners read this script: Yesterday evening I was sitting in the cyber café. My cousin was printing her homework. A stranger was asking for her photograph. The owner was telling him to leave.

2. Write every past progressive verb you hear.

3. In pairs, add one sentence of your own beginning with the words While I was.

4. Read the sentences to another pair and ask them to name the helper, was or were.

PAGE 14: Lesson 2: The past progressive aspect — Summary

## Practice

1. Complete: At 8 o'clock last night, I ________ (do) homework on the computer.

2. Correct the helper: They was sharing one tablet.

3. Complete with when: Father was reading the news ________ the power went off.

4. Write a past progressive sentence about a safe action you were doing yesterday.

## Answers to practice

1. was doing

2. They were sharing one tablet.

3. when

4. Any correct sentence, for example: I was reading a story with my sister.

## Summary
• The past progressive is was or were plus a verb ending in -ing.
• Use was with I, he, she and it, and were with you, we and they.
• Use it for a longer past action, and the simple past for a short action that interrupts it.

PAGE 15: Lesson 3: Using both aspects when we speak and write

LESSON 3: USING BOTH ASPECTS WHEN WE SPEAK AND WRITE
====================================================

## What you will learn
• Pick out present and past progressive forms in a spoken text.
• Choose the aspect that matches the time of the action.
• Use both aspects in a short role play.

Curriculum outcomes: b) use the present and past progressive aspect correctly in oral and written contexts for self- expression; c) adopt the use of the present and past progressive aspect in communication

## Introduction
A reporter can say, I am standing outside the shop, and then say, Yesterday a child was talking to a stranger here. One sentence is now. The other is a past moment still in progress. Listeners need both.

PAGE 16: Lesson 3: Using both aspects when we speak and write — A programme to listen to

## Notes

### A programme to listen to
Read this school-radio script aloud with a partner.

Good afternoon. You are listening to School Air. I am standing outside a cyber café. Children are typing their homework. One boy is asking the owner before he downloads a file. Yesterday at this hour, a girl was chatting with a stranger. Her brother was walking past the door. He told her to stop, and she closed the page. Today the owner is reminding every child to ask an adult first.

Present progressive forms: are listening, am standing, are typing, is asking, is reminding. Past progressive forms: was chatting, was walking. Told and closed are simple past. They are finished actions, so they do not take was or were.

PAGE 17: Lesson 3: Using both aspects when we speak and write — Why we keep using these forms

### Choosing the right aspect
Ask two questions before you write the verb.

1. Is the action in progress, or is it a finished event or a habit?
2. Is the time now, or is it in the past?

If it is in progress now, choose the present progressive. If it was in progress in the past, choose the past progressive. If it is a habit, choose the simple present: I check the sender every time. If it is a finished event, choose the simple past: She closed the page.

### Why we keep using these forms
Showing the time of an action makes a story or a warning clear. I was sharing my password is not the same as I am sharing my password. One happened before. The other is happening now and should be stopped at once. When you speak, match the helper to the subject and finish the main verb with -ing. When you write, read the sentence once more and underline the progressive verb.

Newspapers and magazines use the same forms. This morning, pupils are learning about safe websites. Yesterday, a class was visiting the computer room. Finding the forms in real texts will make your own sentences more confident.

PAGE 18: Lesson 3: Using both aspects when we speak and write — Example 1

## Key words
• role play — acting a short scene as if you are the people in it
• aspect — the form of a verb that shows whether an action is in progress

## Worked examples

### Example 1
In the radio script, is the phrase was chatting present progressive or past progressive?

Working:
1. The helper is was, which is the past of is.
2. The main verb ends in -ing.

Answer: Past progressive

## Worked examples

### Example 2
Complete correctly: Right now the pupils ________ (learn) about passwords. Yesterday we ________ (watch) a short video.

Working:
1. The pupils is plural, so use are plus learning.
2. Yesterday and we need were plus watching.

Answer: The pupils are learning about passwords. Yesterday we were watching a short video.

PAGE 19: Lesson 3: Using both aspects when we speak and write — Cyber café role play

## Activity: Cyber café role play
You will need: The radio script, A notebook for completed sentences

1. In groups of four, role-play a scene at a cyber café. One learner is the owner, one is a child, one is a parent, and one is a stranger sending a message.

2. Each speaker must use at least one present progressive sentence about what is happening now and one past progressive sentence about yesterday.

3. The listeners write the progressive verbs they hear.

4. Complete these sentences together: The child is ________. Yesterday the child was ________. While the owner was ________, the parent ________.

PAGE 20: Lesson 3: Using both aspects when we speak and write — Summary

## Practice

1. Name the aspect in this sentence: Children are typing their homework.

2. Name the aspect in this sentence: Her brother was walking past the door.

3. Choose the better sentence for a habit: I am checking messages every morning, or I check messages every morning.

4. Write one present progressive sentence and one past progressive sentence about using a phone safely.

## Answers to practice

1. Present progressive

2. Past progressive

3. I check messages every morning.

4. Examples: I am asking my father before I click. Yesterday I was reading a message with my mother.

## Summary
• Listen for am, is, are, was or were plus an -ing verb.
• Choose present progressive for now and past progressive for a past action in progress.
• Clear aspect shows whether an action is happening or already happened.

PAGE 21: Revision quiz

REVISION QUIZ
=============

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. Which sentence is in the present progressive?
   A. She downloads songs every day.
   B. She is downloading a song now.
   C. She downloaded a song yesterday.
   D. She was downloading a song.

2. Which helper goes with They?
   A. am
   B. is
   C. are
   D. be

3. What is the -ing form of care?
   A. careing
   B. caring
   C. carreing
   D. cares

4. What is the -ing form of chat?
   A. chating
   B. chatting
   C. chatying
   D. chated

5. Which sentence is past progressive?
   A. I closed the page.
   B. I was closing the page.
   C. I am closing the page.
   D. I close the page.

6. Choose the correct sentence.
   A. They was typing.
   B. They were typing.
   C. They is typing.
   D. They am typing.

7. I was reading a message when the screen went dark. Which action was already in progress?
   A. the screen went dark
   B. I was reading
   C. both finished together
   D. neither action

8. Which word often introduces a longer action happening at the same time?
   A. while
   B. yesterday only
   C. because
   D. hello

9. Why do we show whether an action is happening now or was happening?

10. Complete: Right now we ________ (learn) verb aspect.

PAGE 22: Quiz answers

ANSWERS
=======

1. B. She is downloading a song now.
   Is downloading uses is plus an -ing verb for an action happening now.

2. C. are
   They takes are in the present progressive: They are listening.

3. B. caring
   Care ends in a silent e, so drop the e before -ing.

4. B. chatting
   Chat ends with one vowel and one consonant, so double the t.

5. B. I was closing the page.
   Was closing is was plus an -ing verb.

6. B. They were typing.
   A plural subject takes were in the past progressive.

7. B. I was reading
   Was reading is the longer action. Went dark is the short interrupting event.

8. A. while
   While often introduces an action in progress beside another action.

9. So the listener or reader knows the time of the action and understands the message clearly.
   Aspect stops a past warning and a present action from being confused.

10. are learning
   We takes are, and learn becomes learning.

2. watch adds -ing.
3. Join the two parts.

Answer: The children are watching a cyber-safety video.

## Worked examples

### Example 2
Spell the -ing form of share, chat and download.

Working:
1. share ends in silent e, so drop e.
2. chat is a short verb ending in one vowel and one consonant, so double t.
3. download just adds -ing.

Answer: sharing, chatting, downloading

studyPages.title: Lesson 1: The present progressive aspect — Actions happening now
studyPages.body:
## Activity: Actions happening now
You will need: Verb cards: type, share, use, sit, take, chat, download, help, Notebook

1. In groups, pick four verb cards and write a present progressive sentence for each one about using a phone or computer safely.

2. One learner acts an action, such as typing or closing a laptop, while the group says the sentence: She is typing.

3. Read the sentences aloud and underline am, is or are and the -ing word.

4. Correct any spelling of the -ing form together.

studyPages.title: Lesson 1: The present progressive aspect — Summary
studyPages.body:
## Practice

1. Complete: Look! Father ________ (charge) the phone.

2. Write the -ing form of use, stop and play.

3. Which sentence shows an action happening now: I download songs every Friday, or I am downloading a song now?

4. Make the sentence negative: They are sharing the password.

## Answers to practice

1. is charging

2. using, stopping, playing

3. I am downloading a song now.

4. They are not sharing the password.

## Summary
• The present progressive is am, is or are plus a verb ending in -ing.
• Drop a silent e, and double a final consonant in short verbs such as chat.
• Use it for actions in progress now, not for regular habits.

studyPages.title: Lesson 2: The past progressive aspect
studyPages.body:
LESSON 2: THE PAST PROGRESSIVE ASPECT
=====================================

## What you will learn
• Form the past progressive with was or were and a verb ending in -ing.
• Use it for an action that was in progress at a time in the past.
• Join a past progressive action to a shorter past action with when or while.

Curriculum outcomes: a) identify the present and past progressive forms of the verb in oral and written texts for communication; b) use the present and past progressive aspect correctly in oral and written contexts for self- expression

## Introduction
Yesterday at six o'clock you were not frozen in one finished act. You were eating, walking or reading. The past progressive lets you talk about that unfinished moment in the past.

studyPages.title: Lesson 2: The past progressive aspect — Building the past progressive
studyPages.body:
## Notes

### Building the past progressive
The past progressive uses **was** or **were** plus the -ing form of the main verb. The spelling of the -ing form follows the same rules as in the present progressive.

- I **was** reading a message.
- He **was** uploading a picture.
- You **were** waiting for the page to open.
- The children **were** using the laptop together.

Use **was** with I, he, she, it and one name. Use **were** with you, we, they and plural names.

### What it means
This aspect shows an action that was already happening at a certain time in the past. At 7 o'clock I was watching a learning video. The video was in progress at that time. It does not tell us the moment the video finished.

studyPages.title: Lesson 2: The past progressive aspect — Key words
studyPages.body:
### A long action and a short action
A shorter finished action often interrupts the longer one. Use the past progressive for the longer action and the simple past for the short one.

- I **was downloading** a file when the lights **went** off.
- While Mother **was cooking**, my brother **sent** a message to a stranger.

**While** often introduces the longer action. **When** often introduces the shorter one. Both actions can be progressive if they happened side by side: While I was typing, my sister was drawing.

### Negatives and questions
I was not chatting online. Were you using earphones? After a question, answer with the same helper: Yes, I was. No, they were not.

Do not mix the helpers. She were typing and They was typing are not correct. Match was and were to the subject.

## Key words
• past progressive — was or were plus a verb ending in -ing, for an action in progress in the past
• interrupt — to break into a longer action with a shorter one
• while — a linking word often used for two actions happening at the same time

studyPages.title: Lesson 2: The past progressive aspect — What was happening?
studyPages.body:
## Worked examples

### Example 1
Join the ideas: Neema was closing the laptop. A message appeared.

Working:
1. The closing was already in progress, so keep the past progressive.
2. The message was a short finished event, so use the simple past appeared.
3. Link them with when.

Answer: Neema was closing the laptop when a message appeared.

## Worked examples

### Example 2
Choose was or were: The two boys ________ searching for a safe website.

Working:
1. The subject is plural: two boys.
2. Plural subjects take were.

Answer: were

## Activity: What was happening?
You will need: A short radio or video clip chosen by the teacher, or the class script below, Notebook

1. Listen to a short programme, or listen as two learners read this script: Yesterday evening I was sitting in the cyber café. My cousin was printing her homework. A stranger was asking for her photograph. The owner was telling him to leave.

2. Write every past progressive verb you hear.

3. In pairs, add one sentence of your own beginning with the words While I was.

4. Read the sentences to another pair and ask them to name the helper, was or were.

studyPages.title: Lesson 2: The past progressive aspect — Summary
studyPages.body:
## Practice

1. Complete: At 8 o'clock last night, I ________ (do) homework on the computer.

2. Correct the helper: They was sharing one tablet.

3. Complete with when: Father was reading the news ________ the power went off.

4. Write a past progressive sentence about a safe action you were doing yesterday.

## Answers to practice

1. was doing

2. They were sharing one tablet.

3. when

4. Any correct sentence, for example: I was reading a story with my sister.

## Summary
• The past progressive is was or were plus a verb ending in -ing.
• Use was with I, he, she and it, and were with you, we and they.
• Use it for a longer past action, and the simple past for a short action that interrupts it.

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: Using both aspects when we speak and write
studyPages.body:
LESSON 3: USING BOTH ASPECTS WHEN WE SPEAK AND WRITE
====================================================

## What you will learn
• Pick out present and past progressive forms in a spoken text.
• Choose the aspect that matches the time of the action.
• Use both aspects in a short role play.

Curriculum outcomes: b) use the present and past progressive aspect correctly in oral and written contexts for self- expression; c) adopt the use of the present and past progressive aspect in communication

## Introduction
A reporter can say, I am standing outside the shop, and then say, Yesterday a child was talking to a stranger here. One sentence is now. The other is a past moment still in progress. Listeners need both.

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: Using both aspects when we speak and write — A programme to listen to
studyPages.body:
## Notes

### A programme to listen to
Read this school-radio script aloud with a partner.

Good afternoon. You are listening to School Air. I am standing outside a cyber café. Children are typing their homework. One boy is asking the owner before he downloads a file. Yesterday at this hour, a girl was chatting with a stranger. Her brother was walking past the door. He told her to stop, and she closed the page. Today the owner is reminding every child to ask an adult first.

Present progressive forms: are listening, am standing, are typing, is asking, is reminding. Past progressive forms: was chatting, was walking. Told and closed are simple past. They are finished actions, so they do not take was or were.

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: Using both aspects when we speak and write — Why we keep using these forms
studyPages.body:
### Choosing the right aspect
Ask two questions before you write the verb.

1. Is the action in progress, or is it a finished event or a habit?
2. Is the time now, or is it in the past?

If it is in progress now, choose the present progressive. If it was in progress in the past, choose the past progressive. If it is a habit, choose the simple present: I check the sender every time. If it is a finished event, choose the simple past: She closed the page.

### Why we keep using these forms
Showing the time of an action makes a story or a warning clear. I was sharing my password is not the same as I am sharing my password. One happened before. The other is happening now and should be stopped at once. When you speak, match the helper to the subject and finish the main verb with -ing. When you write, read the sentence once more and underline the progressive verb.

Newspapers and magazines use the same forms. This morning, pupils are learning about safe websites. Yesterday, a class was visiting the computer room. Finding the forms in real texts will make your own sentences more confident.

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: Using both aspects when we speak and write — Example 1
studyPages.body:
## Key words
• role play — acting a short scene as if you are the people in it
• aspect — the form of a verb that shows whether an action is in progress

## Worked examples

### Example 1
In the radio script, is the phrase was chatting present progressive or past progressive?

Working:
1. The helper is was, which is the past of is.
2. The main verb ends in -ing.

Answer: Past progressive

## Worked examples

### Example 2
Complete correctly: Right now the pupils ________ (learn) about passwords. Yesterday we ________ (watch) a short video.

Working:
1. The pupils is plural, so use are plus learning.
2. Yesterday and we need were plus watching.

Answer: The pupils are learning about passwords. Yesterday we were watching a short video.

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: Using both aspects when we speak and write — Cyber café role play
studyPages.body:
## Activity: Cyber café role play
You will need: The radio script, A notebook for completed sentences

1. In groups of four, role-play a scene at a cyber café. One learner is the owner, one is a child, one is a parent, and one is a stranger sending a message.

2. Each speaker must use at least one present progressive sentence about what is happening now and one past progressive sentence about yesterday.

3. The listeners write the progressive verbs they hear.

4. Complete these sentences together: The child is ________. Yesterday the child was ________. While the owner was ________, the parent ________.

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: Using both aspects when we speak and write — Summary
studyPages.body:
## Practice

1. Name the aspect in this sentence: Children are typing their homework.

2. Name the aspect in this sentence: Her brother was walking past the door.

3. Choose the better sentence for a habit: I am checking messages every morning, or I check messages every morning.

4. Write one present progressive sentence and one past progressive sentence about using a phone safely.

## Answers to practice

1. Present progressive

2. Past progressive

3. I check messages every morning.

4. Examples: I am asking my father before I click. Yesterday I was reading a message with my mother.

## Summary
• Listen for am, is, are, was or were plus an -ing verb.
• Choose present progressive for now and past progressive for a past action in progress.
• Clear aspect shows whether an action is happening or already happened.

studyPages.title: Revision quiz
studyPages.body:
REVISION QUIZ
=============

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. Which sentence is in the present progressive?
   A. She downloads songs every day.
   B. She is downloading a song now.
   C. She downloaded a song yesterday.
   D. She was downloading a song.

2. Which helper goes with They?
   A. am
   B. is
   C. are
   D. be

3. What is the -ing form of care?
   A. careing
   B. caring
   C. carreing
   D. cares

4. What is the -ing form of chat?
   A. chating
   B. chatting
   C. chatying
   D. chated

5. Which sentence is past progressive?
   A. I closed the page.
   B. I was closing the page.
   C. I am closing the page.
   D. I close the page.

6. Choose the correct sentence.
   A. They was typing.
   B. They were typing.
   C. They is typing.
   D. They am typing.

7. I was reading a message when the screen went dark. Which action was already in progress?
   A. the screen went dark
   B. I was reading
   C. both finished together
   D. neither action

8. Which word often introduces a longer action happening at the same time?
   A. while
   B. yesterday only
   C. because
   D. hello

9. Why do we show whether an action is happening now or was happening?

10. Complete: Right now we ________ (learn) verb aspect.

studyPages.title: Quiz answers
studyPages.body:
ANSWERS
=======

1. B. She is downloading a song now.
   Is downloading uses is plus an -ing verb for an action happening now.

2. C. are
   They takes are in the present progressive: They are listening.

3. B. caring
   Care ends in a silent e, so drop the e before -ing.

4. B. chatting
   Chat ends with one vowel and one consonant, so double the t.

5. B. I was closing the page.
   Was closing is was plus an -ing verb.

6. B. They were typing.
   A plural subject takes were in the past progressive.

7. B. I was reading
   Was reading is the longer action. Went dark is the short interrupting event.

8. A. while
   While often introduces an action in progress beside another action.

9. So the listener or reader knows the time of the action and understands the message clearly.
   Aspect stops a past warning and a present action from being confused.

10. are learning
   We takes are, and learn becomes learning.
